drivingQuestion: Is a convert obligated in the priestly gifts of his cow when it is uncertain whether it was slaughtered before or after his conversion?
outcomeNote: An unattributed mishna stating a rule with its ground; no party acts on another party's words.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר וְהָיְתָה לוֹ פָּרָה, נִשְׁחֲטָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּיֵּיר – פָּטוּר, מִשֶּׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר – חַיָּיב, סָפֵק – פָּטוּר, שֶׁהַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «a convert who converted and he had a cow,» if the cow «was slaughtered before» he «converted,» he is «exempt» from giving the gifts to the priest. If the animal was slaughtered «after he converted,» the convert is «obligated» to give the gifts. If there is «uncertainty» whether it was slaughtered before or after the conversion, the convert is «exempt, as the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.»

moves.summary: Rules that the convert is exempt if the cow was slaughtered before his conversion and obligated if after.

moves.cueHe: ספק – פטור, שהמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה
moves.summary: In a case of uncertainty he is exempt, since the burden of proof rests on the claimant.
